title: A tooth-enamel-inspired amorphous NiW-ZrO 2 film with enhanced mechanical properties and corrosion resistance.
byline: Wang Z, Yang X, Li B, et al.
html: Metal-ceramic film is widely used in micro-electromechanical devices and surface protective coatings, owing to its micrometer-thick two-dimensional morphology for high processability and depositability, and its high stiffness and hardness compared with metal film for high damage resistance. However, the existing metal-ceramic films are inherently plagued by a persistent trade-off between stiffness and damping, generating a significant decrease in the mechanical dissipation ability of these hybrid films compared with metal films. Simultaneously promoting the stiffness and damping of a ceramic-metal film remains challenging. Inspired by the hierarchical structure of enamel rods and interrod enamel in natural tooth enamel, we constructed a tooth-enamel-inspired fully amorphous NiW-ZrO 2 film through the electrochemically assisted infiltration of an amorphous NiW alloy into amorphous ZrO 2 nanotube arrays. The excellent inherent mechanical properties of amorphous materials and the structural confinement effect of the nanotube array on the amorphous alloy ensure strong structural support and promote the crystallization of the amorphous alloy to dissipate energy, realizing high stiffness ( E ', ∼194 GPa) and high damping (tan δ , ∼0.066) at the same time. The viscoelastic figure of merit (VFOM, ∼12.8 GPa) of the film exceeds that of existing metal, ceramic and metal-based composites. Furthermore, the amorphous NiW-ZrO 2 film exhibits enhanced wear resistance and corrosion resistance under acidic, alkaline, and saline environments. This research proposes a bioinspired approach for developing a high-performance metal-ceramic film that exhibits high stiffness, high damping, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance.
